scope: J009 RLS to rust-analyzer architecture history

events.significance: RLS already targets low-latency incomplete-source IDE work through compiler reuse, database/work queue, and proposed lazy/persistent compilation.
Compiler-as-library becomes the official architectural direction for Rust language-server work.

events.event: RLS matures around rustc save-analysis and build orchestration
events.significance: Precise compiler facts are indexed cross-crate, but semantic refresh remains tied substantially to crate/build work; VFS, cancellation/squashing and Racer fallbacks mitigate but do not remove that shape.

events.event: rust-analyzer begins as error-resilient parsing experiment and grows into useful IDE
events.significance: Separate front-end provides a laboratory for editor-first semantics and state.

events.event: IDE team compares RLS and rust-analyzer
events.significance: RLS precision is contrasted with rust-analyzer performance/flexible API; hybrid save-analysis plus long-term library-ification is considered.

events.event: rust-analyzer first-release account and RFC 2912 start
events.significance: Persistent on-demand queries are presented as a fundamental architecture shift; semantic limitations are acknowledged.
Rust chooses rust-analyzer transition while explicitly accepting temporary duplicate semantics and pursuing shared libraries.
Organizational ownership catches up with the technical direction.
Rust explicitly attributes replacement to RLS architectural limits for interactive latency/quality.

events.event: rust-analyzer moves more state onto newer salsa, including crate graph
events.significance: Fine-grained persistent incrementality remains a core direction rather than a temporary bridge.

events.event: Current inspected rust-analyzer and rustc-dev-guide revisions
events.significance: Distinct editor/compiler front-end contexts coexist with substantial shared rustc semantic libraries, especially trait solving.
